name: Browse.ai
summary: No-code web scraping and data extraction. Turn any website into an automated data pipeline or spreadsheet automatically.
best_for: ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers
skip_if: you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot
honest_knock: Two honest realities of no-code scraping. Credits burn faster than expected: row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter, so monitor a big site daily and do the math first. And scrapers break when sites redesign: robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month billed annually (12,000 credits/yr), or $48/mo billed monthly
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-11-27 on www.browse.ai/pricing with a plain fetch, with browse.ai/llms.txt, last updated 2026-11-17, read alongside it; first re-verified 2026-09-21) Credit-metered, prices in USD. Free is $0 with 50 credits a month, 2 domains and 3 team members. Personal is $19 a month billed annually ($228 a year, all credits upfront) for 12,000 credits a year, 10 domains and 3 team members. Professional is $69 a month billed annually ($828 a year) for 60,000 credits a year, 50 domains and 10 team members. Premium starts at $500 a month billed annually, with custom credits, unlimited domains and Browse AI's own data engineers building the robots; the page quotes Premium volume 'from $0.010 a credit'. The amounts are the same as on 21 September 2026, but the allowances moved: that day the page sold 5 websites on Personal and 10 on Professional. A domain includes its subdomains, so company.com/pricing, help.company.com and jobs.company.com count as one. Month to month, the page's own FAQ data gives Personal at $48 and Professional at $87; the monthly credit buckets sit behind a toggle this reading could not operate (on 21 September they were 2,000 and 5,000 credits a month). The FAQ says annual billing saves 20%, which it puts at $216 a year on Professional and $120 on Personal at the same volume. Our sum for Professional: $87 x 12 = $1,044 against $828, a $216 difference or 20.7%. The comparison table gives the plan cost per credit as $0.019 on Personal and $0.014 to $0.011 on Professional, and the credit range per plan as 12K to 24K a year on Personal and 60K to 360K on Professional. Credit top-ups cost more than plan credits: $0.024 a credit on Personal and $0.017 to $0.013 on Professional, annual plans only, 1,000 credits minimum. Extra domains are $4 a month on Personal and $2.40 on Professional, paid annually. Setup and onboarding by Browse AI's team is from $399, on annual Professional and Premium plans only. Every paid plan now carries a 60-day refund guarantee. Credits reset at the end of the billing cycle and do not roll over; when they run out, robots pause rather than run up a bill; a plan change charges the new plan in full and starts a fresh billing period. Data retention is 90 days on the three self-serve plans and the maximum task run time is 60 minutes. The monitoring line contradicts itself: the banner says monitoring every 5 minutes on every plan, the comparison table says every minute on all four, and the FAQ says frequency runs from every five minutes to monthly. On 21 September the page gave hourly on Free and 5 minutes on paid plans. The older inconsistency in llms.txt, which listed Starter $49, Professional $149 and Team $399 plans, is gone: the file now names Free, Personal, Professional and Premium and says Starter and Team are out of date. The bigger in-plan credit buckets we read on 14 September 2026 (Personal 24,000 credits a year at $38/mo, Professional 120,000 at $129, 240,000 at $239 and 360,000 at $319) sit behind a selector this reading could not operate, so they stay dated 14 September and not re-checked; the FAQ's $120 saving on Personal matches the $38 tier ($48 x 12 = $576 against $38 x 12 = $456).

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Browse AI on the Free plan: a monitored robot trained with Table Studio on a public practice site. Monitor for changes on books.toscrape.com, category Travel. Table Studio trained itself (Extracting the data, 2 of 3) and after about 35 seconds returned a table called Books List with 11 rows and the columns Position, Title, Price, Availability, Rating, URL and Cover Image, with Extract Date 2026-11-13 16:59. The tester checked the result against the live page with curl: all 11 prices were identical, and the category holds exactly 11 books. Save Robot asked how often the robot should check for changes (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly); Daily was chosen, and the email on data changes was set to No. The robot saved and captured fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then showed Default monitor, Every day, No changes. History showed Finished successfully with 11 rows and 1.10 credits. The table has Export and Integrate buttons, which were not used. The first robot was trained free and the first run cost 1.10 credits; at one run a day this list uses about 33 credits a month by the tester arithmetic, inside the 60 credits of Free. Larger lists and more pages were not tested. Whether the monitor survives a redesign of the target site was not tested; it was only seen that the monitor reads the live page on every run. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app shows 60 monthly credits on Free where the review dossier listed 50. Pricing beyond the first run depends on list length, at 0.10 credits per item beyond ten.

sessions.what: We trained one monitored robot on Browse AI's Free plan on 13 November 2026, using its AI-assisted Table Studio on a public practice shop, books.toscrape.com, category Travel. The account is ours, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We joined an existing Free account, so we did not see sign-up. We did not test export, integrations, support, checkout or cancellation.
findings: The start screen offered 'Extract structured data' or 'Monitor for changes'. We chose monitoring. Three training methods followed: Table Studio (AI training, labelled Beta), Robot Studio (point and click) and a Chrome extension. We used Table Studio and installed nothing. No card was requested.

Table Studio trained itself and returned a table called Books List after about 35 seconds (our approximate timing, not a benchmark): 11 rows with position, title, price, availability, rating, URL and cover image. We checked the result against the live page. All 11 prices matched, and the category holds exactly 11 books.

Save Robot asked how often to check for changes: hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. We chose daily and switched email alerts on data changes off. The robot saved and fetched fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then read 'Every day, No changes'.

Training the robot was free. The first run, 11 rows, cost 1.10 credits in the task history. That fits the pricing line of 1 credit per task with 10 list items included plus 0.10 per extra item. At one run a day this list would use about 33 credits a month (our own arithmetic), inside the free allowance.
The billing page showed 60 monthly credits on Free, for 2 websites, with 58.90 available after the first run. Our dossier had said 50, so we corrected it to what the app shows.

The plan cards offered yearly billing with 20% off and all credits paid upfront: Personal $19 a month, Professional $69 a month, Premium from $500 a month. We did not see monthly prices and opened no checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.
not_tested: Sign-up on a fresh account (we joined an existing one)
Larger lists, several pages, and what the monitor does after a redesign of the target site
Email alerts, the Export and Integrate buttons, and the Chrome extension
Support, invitations, roles, API use, downgrade and cancelling
